spine_role: The condensed 'Map' unit for the boredom corpus: it is the editorial/textual apparatus, not lecture argument. Two payloads matter for the boredom spine. (1) The Editor's Epilogue records that Heidegger himself, in working sessions, repeatedly 'emphasized the detailed analysis of boredom' and tied the inaugural lecture 'What Is Metaphysics?' (24 July 1929) — where the attunement of boredom is first treated — to Part One's threefold boredom analysis. (2) The Glossary fixes the canonical McNeill–Walker German↔English equivalents for the entire boredom/world/attunement vocabulary (Langeweile, Stimmung, Benommenheit, Genommenheit, Hingehaltenheit, Leergelassenheit, Augenblick, weltarm, etc.), making it the terminological key for every other unit.

sections.title: For Eugen Fink on His Sixtieth Birthday
Postscript to the Second Edition (F.-W. von Herrmann, March 1992)

section_map.heading: For Eugen Fink on His Sixtieth Birthday
section_map.gist: Heidegger's birthday speech for Eugen Fink (delivered 10 Dec 1965, Viktoria Hotel, Freiburg; speech-text dated Freiburg 30 March 1966). Three 'signs' of the long friendship: the writing-desk move 37 years prior; Fink's name (no. 14) underlined in red in Heidegger's 1928-29 winter-semester upper-seminar list ('These students are likely to achieve something'); shared upper-Swabian origins and Greek/Latin teachers in Constance. Develops the Nietzsche saying 'One repays a teacher badly if one always remains merely a student' (Zarathustra, 'Of the Bestowing Virtue') and an end-of-philosophy / end-of-thinking meditation: philosophy dissipating into the sciences and being overpowered by cybernetics; 'the end of philosophy is not the end of thinking.' Gift: Valéry's 'The Young Parca' (trans. Celan). NOTE: this Appendix opens already on p.366, interleaved in the right column of the 366/367 spread, while the left column still carries the close of §76.

section_map.heading: Editor's Epilogue
section_map.gist: F.-W. von Herrmann's account of the manuscript and editorial principles — the bibliographically load-bearing text. The course title was 'The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics: World, Finitude, Solitude'; delivered four hours/week, WS 1929-30, Freiburg. Brocker and Petzet report the noticeboard subtitle read 'World, Finitude, Individuation,' not 'Solitude'; the manuscript subtitle ('Solitude') was retained. Volume renumbered from prospectus Vol. 30 to the double issue 29-30. Manuscript = 94 sides, horizontal folio, main text on the left-hand side with insertions/remarks on the right. Sources: Guzzoni's early-1960s typescript (DFG grant), Simon Moser's shorthand record, plus Heidegger's personally annotated copy with a closing list of basic words/concepts. The editor deciphered, supplemented from notes Heidegger authorized, divided continuous text into paragraphs, supplied punctuation, and formed all titles except three Heidegger-given ones (the Part One title 'Awakening a Fundamental Attunement in Our Philosophizing,' the Part Two title 'What Is World?,' and §44 'Summary and renewed introduction following the vacation'). Heidegger rejected a subject index. KEY BOREDOM EVIDENCE: at the time of preparing the Gesamtausgabe Heidegger 'repeatedly directed the conversation toward this lecture course, and emphasized the detailed analysis of boredom, in addition to the significance of the course for the concept of world'; and the inaugural Freiburg lecture 'What Is Metaphysics?' (24 July 1929) is named as the first place he 'dealt with the attunement of boredom,' to be read alongside Part One. Also: the Leibniz sentence ascribed on German p.24 could not be located; the dedication of the volume to Fink (d. 25 June 1975) is explained. Signed F.-W. v. Herrmann, Freiburg, December 1982.

section_map.heading: Postscript to the Second Edition
section_map.gist: Corrects the first edition's claim about the SS 1929 course 'Introduction to Academic Study' (intended Vol. 29). After publication, two transcripts surfaced (Herbert Marcuse; Alois Siggemann), so the Epilogue's 'not even worked out in manuscript form' conclusion 'proved to be incorrect.' The editor reconstructs his three lines of inquiry (negative archive search; two attendees with no recollection; Heidegger's own list 'Lectures and Seminars since the Publication of Sein und Zeit (all those fully worked out)' which omitted the course). The two transcripts (nine and seventeen typed pages) show the course concerned the essence of science and philosophy and Plato's cave allegory (Republic Bk VII), but are too short to reconstruct/edit. Signed F.-W. v. Herrmann, Freiburg, March 1992. Note: minor typographical errors of the first edition were corrected for the second.

section_map.heading: Glossary
section_map.gist: A two-page German↔English term list (entries run English-headword: German-equivalent). It fixes the McNeill–Walker renderings for the whole boredom/world/attunement apparatus and is the terminological key for the other units. Boredom cluster: '(profound) boredom: (tiefe) Langeweile'; 'to be bored with...: sich langweilen mit/bei...'; 'to become bored by...: gelangweiltwerden von...'; 'boring: langweilig'; 'the while: die Weile'; 'to drag: zögern' / 'time as it drags: der zögernde Zeitverlauf'; 'to endure: währen' / 'during: während'. Attunement cluster: '(fundamental) attunement: (Grund)stimmung'; 'to attune: stimmen'; '(mood of) melancholy: Schwermut'; '(mood of) courage: Mut'. Captivation/animal cluster: 'captivation: Benommenheit' / 'captivated: benommen', also 'benumbment: Benommenheit' / 'benumbed: benommen'; 'to disinhibit: enthemmen' / 'disinhibition: Enthemmung'; 'encircling ring: Umring' / 'ring: Ring' / 'to encircle: umringen'; 'poor in world: weltarm' / 'poverty in world: Weltarmut'; '(instinctual) drive: Trieb' / 'driven activity: Treiben, Umtrieb'. Structural-moment cluster of profound boredom: '(being) held in limbo: Hingehaltenheit'; '(telling) refusal: Versagen' / 'to refuse: versagen'; '(being) left empty: Leergelassenheit'; 'moment of vision: Augenblick'; 'to entrance: bannen' / 'entrancement: Bann'; 'withholding: Genommenheit'; 'to oppress: bedrängen' / 'oppressiveness: Bedrängnis'; 'compulsion, compelling force: Zwang'. Temporal cluster: 'the standing now: das stehende Jetzt'; 'standing time: die stehende Zeit'; 'to temporalize: sich zeitigen'; 'the now: das Jetzt'; 'temporality: Zeitlichkeit'; 'moment of vision: Augenblick'. World/Dasein cluster: 'world: Welt' / 'world-forming: weltbildend' / 'worldless: weltlos' / '(world-)formation: (Welt-)bildung'; 'individuation: Vereinzelung'; 'solitude: Einsamkeit'; 'finitude: Endlichkeit'; 'proper authenticity: Eigentlichkeit'. NOTE: this OCR omits the headword 'Dasein' and 'Befindlichkeit' — neither appears as an entry in the legible glossary text (gap flagged).

key_terms.gloss: '(profound) boredom' — the canonical McNeill–Walker rendering of the attunement at the heart of Part One; Lang(e)-Weile = the 'long while'.
'to be bored with...' — the first/superficial form's idiom (boredom by some determinate thing).
'to become bored by...' — the second form's passive idiom (being made bored by a situation).
'the while' — the temporal stem inside Lange-weile; the duration one must 'pass' or 'endure'.
'(fundamental) attunement' — the genus under which profound boredom is the privileged fundamental attunement of FCM.
'to attune' — the verb of being-tuned; an attuned being can be otherwise-attuned, hence awakened.
'(mood of) melancholy' — the attunement in which philosophy as creative activity stands (§44 guideline 7).
'captivation' / 'benumbment' — the animal's mode of being (poor in world); glossed twice (captivated/benumbed = benommen).
'disinhibition' — the animal's relation to its disinhibiting ring; to disinhibit = enthemmen.
'(being) held in limbo' — first structural moment of profound boredom (being-held-in-limbo by time's refusal).
'(being) left empty' — the being-left-empty that pairs with being-held-in-limbo in the boredom structure.
'(telling) refusal' — time's telling refusal of beings as a whole in profound boredom; to refuse = versagen.
'moment of vision' — the liberating moment announced within profound boredom; the temporal point of resolute disclosedness.
'entrancement' / 'to entrance' — the entrancement of time's horizon characterizing profound boredom.
'withholding' — the withholding/being-taken structure feeding the Benommenheit (captivation) and Hingenommenheit ('being taken') family.

key_terms.term: das stehende Jetzt / die stehende Zeit
key_terms.gloss: 'the standing now' / 'standing time' — the arrested temporality disclosed in profound boredom.
'poor in world' / 'poverty in world' — the animal thesis; Armut shares the Mut root flagged at §44.
'world-forming' / 'worldless' — the man and stone theses of the world-comparison.
'individuation' — the noticeboard subtitle the Epilogue says Heidegger preferred ('World, Finitude, Individuation').

Within the Appendix Heidegger invokes the Greek beginning of Western thinking 'prepared by poetry'; the Nietzsche/Zarathustra 'intoxicated song' frames world as 'deep.' (No standalone Greek glossary entry; world-history motif only.)

claims.text: Heidegger himself 'emphasized the detailed analysis of boredom, in addition to the significance of the course for the concept of world' during the GA editing sessions — external authorial confirmation that boredom is the course's centerpiece.

The inaugural Freiburg lecture 'What Is Metaphysics?' (24 July 1929) is where Heidegger 'dealt with the attunement of boredom for the first time'; Part One's threefold boredom analysis 'must be read in the context of this inaugural lecture.'
The course's announced noticeboard subtitle was 'World, Finitude, Individuation,' not 'Solitude' (per Brocker and Petzet); the manuscript subtitle 'Solitude' was nonetheless retained for publication.

The volume was renumbered from the prospectus's Vol. 30 to the double issue 29-30 because the SS 1929 course 'Introduction to Academic Study' (planned Vol. 29) was thought neither held nor drafted — a conclusion the Postscript later retracts.

The manuscript comprises 94 sides in horizontal folio, with the main text written on the left-hand side and insertions/improvements/abbreviated remarks on the right — the same left/right layout the present cache's 2-up split exploits.

Only three titles are Heidegger's own — Part One 'Awakening a Fundamental Attunement in Our Philosophizing,' Part Two 'What Is World?,' and §44 'Summary and renewed introduction following the vacation'; all other chapter/section titles were formed by the editor from Heidegger's phrasings. Heidegger rejected a subject index.

Postscript correction: two transcripts (Herbert Marcuse; Alois Siggemann, nine and seventeen typed pages) surfaced after publication, so the editor's earlier 'not even worked out in manuscript form' verdict on the SS 1929 course 'proved to be incorrect'; that course treated the essence of science/philosophy via Plato's cave (Republic Bk VII).

The Glossary fixes '(profound) boredom: (tiefe) Langeweile' and the full attunement/captivation/temporal vocabulary as the canonical McNeill–Walker equivalences — the terminological key for every boredom unit.

In the Appendix Heidegger frames an 'end of philosophy' under the rise of cybernetics yet insists 'the end of philosophy is not the end of thinking,' connecting the volume's dedication to the friendship with Fink.

interlocutors.name: Eugen Fink
interlocutors.role: Dedicatee of the Appendix and of the whole volume; Husserl student who 'entered another, and yet the same school of phenomenology'; d. 25 June 1975, prompting the posthumous dedication.

interlocutors.name: Friedrich-Wilhelm von Herrmann
interlocutors.role: Volume editor; author of the Editor's Epilogue (Dec 1982) and the Postscript to the Second Edition (March 1992); sets out the manuscript history and editorial principles.

interlocutors.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
interlocutors.role: Cited in the Appendix: Zarathustra's 'intoxicated song' ('The world is deep...') and 'One repays a teacher badly if one always remains merely a student' ('Of the Bestowing Virtue'); also The Will to Power No. 466 on 'the victory of method over science.'

interlocutors.name: Walter Brocker & Heinrich Wiegand Petzet
interlocutors.role: Course attendees whose reports establish the 'Individuation' vs 'Solitude' subtitle discrepancy.

interlocutors.name: Simon Moser
interlocutors.role: Former student whose bound shorthand transcript of the course became Heidegger's annotated 'personal record' used by the editor.

interlocutors.name: Ute Guzzoni
interlocutors.role: Prepared the early-1960s typescript of the manuscript (with a DFG grant Heidegger applied for).

interlocutors.name: Herbert Marcuse & Alois Siggemann
interlocutors.role: Authors of the two SS-1929 transcripts surfacing after publication, forcing the Postscript's retraction.

interlocutors.name: Hermann Heidegger
interlocutors.role: Administrator of Heidegger's estate; consulted on the un-held Vol. 29 course and thanked for editorial consultation.

interlocutors.name: Paul Valéry / Paul Celan
interlocutors.role: Valéry's 'The Young Parca,' translated by Celan, is Heidegger's birthday gift to Fink — marking the poetising-and-thinking motif.

bridge_relevance: This end-matter unit is the corpus's terminological and bibliographic ground truth. The Editor's Epilogue supplies external, author-confirmed warrant that boredom is FCM's centerpiece (Heidegger 'emphasized the detailed analysis of boredom') and anchors it to 'What Is Metaphysics?' (1929) — letting the King-Salvo bridge cite a non-circular reason for treating boredom as the privileged attunement rather than one mood among many. The Glossary pins the exact German↔English equivalents (Langeweile, Stimmung, Benommenheit, Hingehaltenheit, Leergelassenheit, Augenblick, weltarm) that every other unit's quotations depend on, so the bridge's mapping from lab constructs (boredom stimulus, disengagement, captivation/flow) to Heideggerian terms rests on a fixed lexicon.
